deities: Goddess Chaturshringi (also called Ambareshwari, Mahakali, Mahalakshmi, Mahasaraswati)
Durga and Ganesha (shrines in the temple complex)
Ashtavinayaka (eight miniature idols across the four hillocks)
festivals: Navratri (annual fair at the foothills; 15-day Navratri Mahotsav ending with a silver-chariot procession of the goddess on Vijaya Dashami / Dussehra)

history.dynasty: Maratha (built during the Maratha era, Peshwa period; creator Durlabhsheth Pitambardas Mahajan)
history.period: 18th century, during the reign of the Marathas / Peshwas (about 250 years old; some sources attribute it to Shivaji's era)
history.summary: Chaturshringi ('the mountain with four peaks') is a hill temple on Senapati Bapat Road in north-west Pune, considered the presiding goddess of the city of Pune. Legend: the wealthy moneylender and mint-owner Durlabhsheth Pitambardas Mahajan was a devotee of Saptashringi Devi of Vani (near Nashik, ~300 km away) and travelled there annually on the full moon of Chaitra; in old age he could no longer make the journey and prayed in sorrow, and the goddess appeared in his dream saying, 'If you cannot come to me, I will come to you.' Directed to a mountain north-west of Pune, he excavated there and found a natural swayambhu idol of the goddess; he built the temple on the spot, minted a Chaturshringi rupee to celebrate, and Navratri celebrations began there. The temple, 90 feet high and 125 feet wide, reached by over 200 steps, was renovated over time; the deity is maintained by five generations of the Angal family and the Shri Chaturshringi Devasthan Trust. Note: some sources place construction in Shivaji's reign, others in the Peshwa era - the period is not firmly established.

name: Chaturshringi Temple
town_description: Pune is the cultural capital of Maharashtra. The temple is on the slope of a hill on Senapati Bapat Road, near Gokhalenagar and Pune University, in the north-west of the city.

travel.road: On Senapati Bapat Road, well served by city buses, autos, and taxis; over 200 steps climb the hill to the shrine.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri is the grandest time (fair at the foothills with giant wheels and food stalls).
visitor_information.opening_hours: 7:00 AM to 9:00 PM daily (verify). Entry free; Indian traditional dress code expected.
